title: 2009 Bond Helicopters Eurocopter AS332 crash

location.name: North Sea, 11 nm northeast of Peterhead

summary: Bond Offshore Helicopters Flight 85N crashed in the North Sea on 1 April 2009 while returning from a BP oil platform to Aberdeen Airport. The main rotor separated following catastrophic failure of the main rotor gearbox. A fatigue fracture of a second stage planet gear in the epicyclic module caused the gearbox failure. Metallic debris had been detected on the gearbox chip detector 36 flying hours before the accident but was not recognized as indicating degradation requiring action.
probable_cause: Catastrophic failure of the main rotor gearbox resulting from fatigue fracture of a second stage planet gear in the epicyclic module. The detection of metallic particles on the chip detector on 25 March 2009 was not recognized as an indication of gear degradation requiring immediate action before the next flight.

factors.evidence: Fatigue fracture of second stage planet gear in epicyclic module caused gearbox failure (p. 1)
Magnetic particle on chip detector not recognized as gear degradation indicator (p. 1)
Main rotor gearbox failure and rotor separation; helicopter crashed with all 16 killed (p. 1)

events.text: 36 flying hours before accident: magnetic particle detected on epicyclic module chip detector during routine inspection (p. 1)
Catastrophic failure of main rotor gearbox during cruise flight from BP Miller platform to Aberdeen (p. 1)
Helicopter crashed 11 nautical miles northeast of Peterhead in North Sea (p. 1)
Investigation confirmed fatigue fracture of second stage planet gear as root cause; metallic debris detection systems inadequate for early warning (p. 1)
All 16 occupants (2 flight crew, 14 passengers/crew) killed in crash and North Sea waters (p. 1)

notes: AAIB Final Report 2/2011; 5 key events extracted
History of flight section reviewed; fatigue failure in gearbox identified as root cause
Chip detector metallic particle detection discussed as contributing factor
